segments.he: בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין וְכוּ׳, אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ וְכוּ׳.
segments.en: § The mishna cites a disagreement between the Rabbis and Rabbi Shimon with regard to temporarily «blemished» animals: Rabbi Shimon holds that one who sacrifices them outside the Temple courtyard violates a prohibition, as they will be fit for sacrifice after the passage of time, whereas the Rabbis hold that one is exempt. The mishna cites two similar disagreements: With regard to doves whose time of fitness has not yet arrived that are slaughtered outside the Temple courtyard, and with regard to one who slaughters an animal «itself and its offspring» on one day, where the latter, which is not fit for being sacrificed until the next day, is slaughtered outside the Temple courtyard.
